<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 10 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">General Relativity</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">10.3</span> Coupling to Matter</h1></header>
<p>Matter enters through its own action, added to <span class="math inline">\(S_\mathcal{D}\)</span>. Varying the matter fields gives their equations on the curved spacetime; varying the metric gives the Einstein equations with a source, the energy-momentum tensor. The Setting is that of Subsection <span class="dg-xref dg-xref-pending" data-label="subsection_EH_variation">10.2.2</span>.</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p><strong>Total action.</strong> For matter fields <span class="math inline">\(\Phi\)</span> (tensor fields on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>) and a scalar field <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_M\)</span> built  from <span class="math inline">\(\Phi\)</span>, its derivatives and <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(S_M[g, \Phi] \coloneqq \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega^g \mathcal{L}_M\)</span>. The total action  <span class="math inline">\(S_\mathcal{D} + S_M\)</span> is required to be critical under two independent kinds of variations: of <span class="math inline">\(\Phi\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> fixed, which  give the <strong>matter field equations</strong>, and of <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\Phi\)</span> fixed.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Energy-momentum tensor.</strong> The response of <span class="math inline">\(S_M\)</span> to a change of the metric defines the symmetric  <span class="math inline">\((0,2)\)</span>-tensor field <span class="math inline">\(T\)</span> (<a class="dg-cite" href="../bibliography.html#bib-Landau_Lifshitz_1975">Landau and Lifshitz, 1975</a>):  <span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
    \frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} S_M[g_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}, \Phi] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0}
    = - \frac{1}{2} \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega^g \, (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}_{ij} ,
    \qquad
    (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} = (g^{-1})^{ia} \, (g^{-1})^{jb} \, T_{ab} ,
    }
    \]</span>  for every admissible <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\)</span>, uniquely by step 5. If <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_M\)</span> contains no derivatives of <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span>, then  <span class="math inline">\(\delta \mathcal{L}_M = \Theta^{ij} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}_{ij}\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\Theta\)</span> symmetric, and panel (A) of Figure <span class="dg-xref dg-xref-pending" data-label="fig_EH_chain_rule">10.3</span>  gives  <span class="math display">\[
    (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} = - 2 \, \Theta^{ij} - \mathcal{L}_M \, (g^{-1})^{ij} ,
    \]</span>  the second term coming from the volume element. Derivatives of <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_M\)</span> are first moved off <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\)</span> as in  step 4.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Einstein equations.</strong> With <span class="math inline">\(- \kappa = 1/(16 \pi G_N)\)</span>, the variation of <span class="math inline">\(S_\mathcal{D} + S_M\)</span> in <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> is  <span class="math inline">\(\int_\mathcal{D} \Omega^g \big( \frac{1}{16 \pi G_N} (\hat{G})^{ij} - \frac{1}{2} (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} \big) \textrm{\runic ᛉ}_{ij}\)</span>, and step 5  gives  <span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
    G = 8 \pi G_N \, T .
    }
    \]</span>  <span class="math inline">\(T\)</span> is to the metric what a current is to the electromagnetic potential: the response of the action to a change of  it. The contracted Bianchi identity (Subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="../proofs-and-additional-material/metric-properties.html#subsection_metric_prop_Bianchi" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_metric_prop_Bianchi">B.18.10</a>) forces  <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{kl} (\nabla_{\partial x_k} T)_{ln} = 0\)</span>, local conservation of energy and momentum, which a chart-independent  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_M\)</span> guarantees through the matter field equations. The normalization of <span class="math inline">\(T\)</span> gives the familiar energy  densities and fluxes, and <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric}_{00} = 4 \pi G_N \rho\)</span> of Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../newtonian/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Newtonian">9</a> in the Newtonian limit.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Example: electromagnetism.</strong> For the potential <span class="math inline">\(\mathsf{A}\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(F_{ij} = \partial_i \mathtt{a}_j - \partial_j \mathtt{a}_i\)</span>  and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{EM}} = - \frac{1}{4} F_{ab} (F^{\flat^{-1}})^{ab}\)</span>, the two kinds of variations give the  <strong>Einstein–Maxwell equations</strong> (Appendix <span class="dg-inprep" title="This part of the notes is in preparation">in preparation</span>)  <span class="math display">\[
    G_{mn} = 8 \pi G_N \Big( - (g^{-1})^{bd} \, F_{mb} \, F_{nd} + \frac{1}{4} \, g_{mn} \, F_{ab} \, (F^{\flat^{-1}})^{ab} \Big),
    \qquad
    (\nabla_{\partial x_a} F^{\flat^{-1}})^{ab} = 0 .
    \]</span></p></li>
</ul>
